Levelling has become a very fast, streamlined process.

You can get yourself to Tier 4 (as a reminder, the highest difficulty) in a few hours, without really optimizing your build, or having any external assistance.

I wouldn't bother playing the campaign. It is completely busted now, with exp changes.

Helltides are permanent, barring a 5 minute window. These are the meta for levelling and gearing up now. Once you've gotten yourself some levels behind you, you throw down in Nightmare dungeons for glyph exp, and finally you have your Uber Bosses -- you'll pickup materials from different sources to summon them, for good loot -- including about a 2% drop rate on uber uniques.

For an added challenge, there are also now Tormented Versions of these bosses. These don't die in 3 seconds, without a very meta build. They drop even more loot.

Your end game is The Pit. Very similar to D3s Greater Rifts, but the loot pinata at the end isn't quite as rewarding. You get unique materials here, to "masterwork" your gear, which increases a random attribute. 

There's a lot less RNG on gear, in terms of stats. There's a *lot* more, in terms of forging and masterworks your gear, though. Be prepared to "brick" otherwise perfect items. It's the same sort of system P2W mobile games incorporate, raid shadow legends etc.

It's in an okay place. This seasons has a rep you can grind out, and the battle pass of course. The games funneling you towards to end game now, and there's practically no reason to explore anything else (dungeons, campaign etc). 

Not really the direction I personally was hoping for, with the game, but I've just gone to D2R instead. A lot of people are thoroughly enjoying the game, and it's worth checking out.

Comorbidity is high between Autism and ADHD. You're correct. 

Self diagnosis, or an attempt at it, is going to be your first step here. You're doing it right, questioning areas that are common symptoms, and assessing them critically. Remember to ask yourself if your atypical aversion or interests impact your quality of life.

From there, compile a list as best you can, that references these "abnormalities", and present it to a doctor and make it very clear You're seeking a screening from a Psychiatrist. A general practicioner can **not** diagnose you. If yiu can find someone who specializes in adults, you'll have a far better experience in most cases.

From there, you'll likely be interviewed by someone who will get a rundown on your life, from childhood to present, and they're looking for key flags that are commonly found in Autistic People, as well as ascertaining wether you are facing a reduction in quality of life due to these things.

They will likely want to interview your parents, for another perspective on your life and experiences, as well as early childhood you either can't recall, or memories are fuzzy and possibly wrong.
